title: Exhaustive target structure and reference documents
question: What is the exact target structure of every package and module, and how is it fixed so phase detail cannot drift from it?

options.text: Exhaustive generated map with Internal namespaces and stable public FQCNs (chosen)
Rules only, placement decided per phase: drift and repeated analysis
Full per-domain re-layout like Chatom (Exceptions/Events per domain): large consumer break without functional gain
Keep internal FQCNs where they are: smaller diff, but boundaries visible only through attributes and harder to scan

context: Independent architecture review (revision 2) requested by the owner (brief M6, M7); the owner asked for the complete package structure and a technical reference that detailing cannot deviate from. Phase tasks and implementation remain deferred.
decision: The per-type placement in knowledge/type-map (generated from the baseline by artifacts/inventory/target_map.py) is the reference for all moves. Rules: publication is the #[Api]/#[Spi] attribute; attributed types live outside \Internal\; internal types live under <Zone>\Internal\ (Sources\<Adapter>\Internal, Filament\Internal\<Area>); published FQCNs stay unless the map lists a move; Kernel values, events, exceptions, enums and Storage\Schema\StorageSchema never move; exceptions stay in one Exceptions namespace; Filament resource pages keep the framework layout with @internal. Module roots: AzGuard\Scopes\, AzGuard\Audit\, AzGuard\DevTools\ under packages/core/modules/<module>/src. knowledge/contracts fixes the signatures of new and changed types; knowledge/identities and knowledge/upgrade-map fix identities and the 0.7.0 map. A deviation requires a decision and a #review entry.
rationale: Rules plus a mixed-area map leave ~420 placements to later sessions, which would re-derive them differently. The ecosystem (Chatom, CoreX, Commerz) keeps implementation under Internal namespaces, which also makes the boundary scans of I2–I4 mechanical. Stable published FQCNs keep the upgrade map short; internal FQCNs carry no promise, so their one-time move is safe. Exceptions and events stay centralized because installed applications catch and listen to them by FQCN.
consequences: P3 moves about 190 internal types and 8 module types once; tests update imports mechanically.
P1 scans use target-map.json as the ownership oracle.
The upgrade map lists only supported symbols.

evidence.note: The owner asked for the complete package structure and a reference without room for deviation.
